newsitem.title: USA: Alcan sees global can stock demand growth.
newsitem.headline: Alcan sees global can stock demand growth.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd expects global demand for aluminum can stock to increase two percent per year from 1996 through 2000, Brian W. Sturgell said Friday.

That is based on its expectation demand for beverage cans will increase three percent per year from 1995 through 2005, he told a news conference. Sturgell is executive vice president, Fabricated Products/North American, for Alcan and president of its U.S. subsidiary, Alcan Aluminum Corp.
Sturgell said North American can demand is expected to actually ease 0.2 percent over the 10 year period.
But European demand is seen up four percent, Asian is seen rising 10 percent and Latin American jumping 18 percent.
He said this will result in demand for 267 billion cans in 2005, up from 193 billion in 1995 and a projected 231 billion in 2000.

Noting the amount of aluminum in each can has declined two percent per year, or 22 percent, since 1986, he said "we're projecting it will continue (to decline) at about 1.8 percent compounded, or another 15 percent" by 2005.

Sturgell said Alcan estimated global aluminum can stock demand slipped to 3.375 million metric tonnes in 1996 from 3.405 million in 1995. The company forecasts total demand of 3.4 million tonnes this year, 3.5 million in 1998, 3.55 million in 1999 and 3.65 million in 2000.
"Our first quarter is very strong," he continued, adding Alcan "did not anticipate some of the strength.
"We're not ready to say it represents ... (anything more than) overdone restocking," he said.
